sentences.text: This massive dinosaur grew to an estimated length of 17 meters, stood 5 meters tall, and weighed approximately 20 tonnes.
The species was formally described in 2005 by a team of Chinese paleontologists led by Peng Guangzhao.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consists of a partial skeleton lacking a skull, discovered in the Dashanpu township of Sichuan, China.
Paleontologists have since recovered numerous additional specimens from the same Dashanpu area.
It was a quadrupedal herbivore, a feeding style consistent with most sauropods.
In 2022, researchers identified Dashanpusaurus as the most basal member of the Macronaria clade.
The animal is classified within the family Camarasauridae.
It belongs to the larger parent group known as Macronaria.
Dashanpusaurus lived approximately 165 million years ago during the Bathonian and Callovian stages of the Middle Jurassic in what is now Asia.
Its time range is estimated to span from 170.9 to 154.8 million years ago.
